function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with a given portion size to track dietary intake. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log, such as 'apple', 'bread', or 'chicken breast'.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, specified in the unit given by portion_unit. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount, such as 'cup', 'grams', or 'slice'.

meal_type.description: The type of meal or snack this food item is being logged for.

log_date.description: The date and time when the food was consumed, in ISO 8601 format such as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'.

message.reasoning:
We need to log foods. We have two meals: earlier (maybe lunch?) and now (maybe snack?). The user didn't specify meal types. Default is snack. But we can infer earlier might be lunch? They said earlier I had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee. That could be lunch. Then later they had 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea. That could be snack. So we should log each item separately. For each call, we need to provide food_name, portion_amount, portion_unit, meal_type optional, log_date optional. We don't have dates; we can omit log_date. We'll use default meal_type if not specified. But we can set meal_type appropriately: earlier -> lunch, later -> snack. Let's do two calls for pizza slices: food_name: "pepperoni pizza slice"? Portion_amount: 2, portion_unit: "slice", meal_type: "lunch". Coffee: food_name: "coffee", portion_amount: 1, portion_unit: "cup", meal_type: "lunch". Mango: food_name: "frozen mango piece", portion_amount: 8, portion_unit: "piece", meal_type: "snack". Chai tea: food_name: "chai tea", portion_amount: 1, portion_unit: "cup", meal_type: "snack".

We need to call the function twice? Actually four times. We can combine multiple logs? The function logs one food item at a time. So we need to make four calls. We'll output them sequentially.
